subject: Hosted inference — service notice: p95 latency spike (US-West)
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: US-West p95 spike — propose statuspage + customer note

Team —

Quick signal this morning: our p95 for generation endpoints in US-West increased from ~220ms to ~780ms starting ~08:40 PT and intermittently persisting. Impact surface: hosted text-generation (v2 models) — mostly customers with synchronous low-latency SLAs. KeystoneRetail is on a higher-sensitivity route and may have observed elongated checkout autocomplete responses.

Immediate asks:
- Can we finalize a short customer-facing blurb and post it to status.redwoodinference.com? I want something up within 30–45m.
- Ben: confirm whether we should activate a temporary routing fallback to us-east for KeystoneRetail (warm pool available).
- Marissa: draft the external email — one short paragraph + bullet mitigations + link to status page.

I've attached an early p95-chart.png (token p95 by minute) — looks correlated with a routing fanout increase around 08:38. Investigating whether a recent kernel selector tweak increased tail latencies for certain sequence length distributions.

I'll hold on the public post until we have wording.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: p95-chart.png (PNG image, 220KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: US-West p95 spike — propose statuspage + customer note

Thanks Vivek — draft below. Kept it brief so we can publish quickly. I also attached a plaintext statuspage-draft.md you can copy into the console.

--- draft start ---
Subject: Service notice — elevated p95 latency (US-West)

Summary: Between ~08:40 PT and ongoing, we observed elevated p95 latency for hosted generation in our US-West region affecting a subset of customers. Some customers may see slower synchronous responses.

What we are doing:
- Routing adjustments to shift traffic to alternate pools (US-East warm pool) for affected customers.
- Reverting a recent kernel selection change for the v2 runtime that correlates with the tail increase.
- Active monitoring with higher alert sensitivity; engineering investigating root cause.

Customer impact: Intermittent p95 increases for generation endpoints. No data loss, requests eventually complete.

Next update: We will post a follow-up on the status page within 2 hours or sooner if we have more details.

--- draft end ---

Ben — if fallback routing is OK, note that the outbound email will say we enabled a temporary reroute for KeystoneRetail to reduce customer impact.

Marissa Cole
Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: statuspage-draft.md (text)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma James <emma.james@keystoneretail.com>, ops@keystoneretail.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted Inference — brief service notice: elevated p95 latency (US-West)

Emma / Keystone ops team —

Wanted to make you aware of a brief service notice: between ~08:40 PT and the present we observed elevated p95 latency for our hosted generation endpoints in the US-West region. You may have seen slower autocomplete and suggestion responses in your integration.

What we’ve done so far:
- Enabled a temporary routing fallback for your account to our US-East warm pool to reduce tail latency.
- Reverted a recent runtime kernel-selector change that correlated with the tail increase.
- Increased monitoring sensitivity and are running targeted load traces to validate fixes.

Impact: intermittent p95 increases — requests continue to complete. We do not see any data loss.

We posted a short incident entry on our status page here: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/RI-2026-05-18-001

Next steps: We expect to have a more detailed update within 2 hours once traces complete and mitigation impact is validated. If you'd like an immediate call, I can schedule a 30-minute sync with engineering now.

Apologies for the disruption — we’re prioritizing this.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-snapshot.json (log excerpt, 45KB)

From: Emma James <emma.james@keystoneretail.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted Inference — brief service notice: elevated p95 latency (US-West)

Thanks for the heads up, Vivek. We saw some intermittent slowdowns in production around that time but responses recovered after ~09:50 PT. Appreciate the fallback to US-East — that should limit user impact.

Can we get a short postmortem once you have traces? Ops would like to understand whether this could recur during Black Friday testing next month.

— Emma
Emma James
Engineering Manager, Platform
KeystoneRetail

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted Inference — brief service notice: elevated p95 latency (US-West)

Posted the statuspage entry and copied the short customer note to customer-comms. Link to incident and internal postmortem draft here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d-internal-postmortem

Initial findings: kernel selector change pushed 08:20 PT weighted an optimized kernel for short sequences that increases variance for mixed sequence workloads. Rolling that change back reduced p95 by ~60% in traces. We left the Keystone fallback in place for 30m and then removed after observing stable p95.

Will leave the postmortem draft in the drive; ETA for final postmortem: EOD tomorrow.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
